headline: High: Devin’s broad workspace and write privileges can drive dangerous cross-agent prompt, data, and action cascades through Flowise flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and use MCP, while Flowise can read/write server files and ingest uploaded files or tool outputs. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if Devin’s outputs are fed into a Flowise flow or datastore. The pair is not provably isolated, but the pathway is not shown as default-manual copy only, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Devin writes content that Flowise later parses as instructions or tool parameters, injection is possible.
IF both are connected through a shared file, datastore, or uploaded artifact, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Devin-generated files into Flowise flows.
Add a provenance tag and allowlist for any file or message passed between the agents.
Use a read-only handoff folder for inter-agent artifacts.
Review Flowise prompts/nodes for instruction-following on untrusted text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets; Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs plus uploaded files and server filesystem. If they share a workspace or handoff path, sensitive code or tokens can flow into Flowise outputs or model-provider calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so medium is the safest choice under uncertainty.
conditions: IF Devin exports code, chat, or tokens into a shared file or upload, Flowise can ingest them.
IF Flowise forwards those inputs to model providers or HTTP tools, sensitive data may leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep Devin and Flowise on separate workspaces or buckets.
Block secrets from being written into shared artifacts.
Turn off or restrict Flowise uploads for sensitive projects.
Add a quick DLP scan on any handoff file before import.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted cloud-workspace shell, filesystem write, and git modification; Flowise can write its server filesystem and operate with broad network egress. They can both mutate shared artifacts if deployed against the same repo or datastore, but the profiles do not prove simultaneous write access to the same path. That makes a real conflict plausible, though not confirmed as high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or server directory, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Flowise flows and Devin sessions target the same mutable resource without locking, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories per agent.
Enable locking or single-writer rules for shared resources.
Require manual merge review for any git changes from Devin.
Avoid concurrent writes to Flowise server files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser, shell, and integrations, while Flowise is a graph-based tool runner that can turn upstream outputs into downstream actions. If Devin’s output is used as Flowise input without verification, errors can cascade into emails, API calls, or commits. Because both agents are action-capable by default, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Flowise consumes Devin-generated text as authoritative input, downstream tool nodes may execute bad actions.
IF Devin supplies incorrect facts or commands and Flowise does not verify them, the error propagates.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before any Flowise action node.
Require schema validation on Devin outputs before Flowise consumes them.
Use a verification node that checks facts against source data.
Disable write-capable Flowise nodes for untrusted upstream inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace; Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and model-provider/tool credentials on a deployment-dependent server. If regulated or sensitive data is routed from Devin into Flowise, retention, residency, or logging policies can diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete certification mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data from Devin is copied into Flowise, the two systems may apply different retention or logging rules.
IF Flowise is deployed in a different jurisdiction or with different provider terms, residency mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before moving it between agents.
Keep regulated data out of Flowise unless deployment terms are reviewed.
Align retention settings and log redaction on both systems.
Document the approved data classes for each agent.
